card.name: Words just before 'numbers' or 'population'
card.fires_on: The word right before an expected 'number(s)' or 'population', such as an adjective (small, low, stable), a possessive or a pronoun. It appears mostly in text about animal counts or study sample sizes.

modes.label: Size adjective before number
modes.description: An adjective like small, low, stable or healthy that leads into 'numbers' or 'sample sizes'.
modes.example: interpretation of changes in pulmonary function test measures in this population are limited due to<< small>> sample sizes.

modes.label: Possessive before numbers
modes.description: An apostrophe or pronoun that points to a group whose numbers or population come next.
modes.example: Just last year scientists projected the animals<<'>> population could fall as low as 5

modes.label: Count label in tables
modes.description: An equals sign in a table note defining N as a number of subjects.
modes.example: N *<< =>> Number of subjects who had assessments at both
